reviews.text: I went here and had the pleasure of meeting D. She’s absolutely amazing and helped us with finding food that all our fish are willing to eat. Great place; and will definitely visit again!!!

Customer service is horrific. They just sit behind the counter and when you ask for something they roll their eyes and act like you’re bothering them.  Will never be returning place also smells.

I called before I drove the hour and 10 minutes to ask if they had the breed and color of the Guppy Fish I wanted. They assured me what I asked for was in stock and abruptly hung up. When I got there, they barely had any guppies and did not have any color or kind I had asked about. Their.stock may be better for for other animals, but, don’t go there for fish.

Unfortunately, the customer service—or what passes for it here.

Employees follow customers around the store so closely that you would think someone had walked in announcing plans to steal an entire snake collection. I understand wanting to prevent theft, but there is a rather significant difference between being attentive and making paying customers feel like they’re under surveillance.

Ironically, while employees seem to have no trouble keeping a very close eye on customers, one employee apparently couldn't manage to keep an eye on where she was walking. She nearly hit my child while walking through an aisle because she wasn't paying attention to her surroundings.

For a store this small, you'd think situational awareness would be one of the easier parts of the job. Apparently, that was an unreasonable expectation.

And then there is the issue of the apparent signal jammer being used inside the store. If a signal jammer is in fact being operated on the premises, that is not something that should simply be brushed aside as another quirky aspect of the shopping experience. It is something that warrants investigation by the appropriate authorities, including the FCC Enforcement Bureau.

What I find particularly fascinating is the contrast between the apparent level of suspicion directed toward customers and the apparent lack of scrutiny applied to the store's own practices.

Perhaps instead of treating every customer like a potential criminal, management should spend some of that energy examining the condition and sourcing of the animals being sold, employee awareness and safety practices, and whether the equipment being used on the premises is actually lawful.

I don't expect perfection from a small business. I do, however, expect basic competence, reasonable customer service, and appropriate standards when live animals and children are involved.

Unfortunately, this store managed to make even those expectations seem ambitious.

If this is how the store treats its customers and handles basic responsibilities, I can't imagine why anyone would feel comfortable trusting them with an animal.

I don't know where our review went. We purchased 3 dumbo rats right after the first of the year, we called before going to reserve 3 baby females and to let them know we would be there in an hour. By the time we got there they had sold one of our babies but offered us a teenager. We shouldn't have taken her but did anyway, we weren't even offered a reduced cost for the one. She was leaking porphyria but they said they were treating her, I asked about a health guarantee and never got an answer and asked what they were treating with. I was told just something they put in the water. Called several times to confirm what treatment was so we could inform our vet at her visit. Never got an answer, either no one knew or the rodent person was out. All 3 were infested with lice. Started our own antibiotic to get her through until the vet visit.  I spent THREE HOURS picking lice and mites off this teenager, then another hour picking them off the babies. Teenager started a steady decline, got to the vet and diagnosed with pneumonia.  I have vet bills of $200 for a rat that passed away from her lice infestation and pneumonia, despite treatment, barely a week after bringing her home. I can provide said invoices for treatment and meds as well as photos of how many bugs I picked off just the teenager. So buyer beware. We will not be back.

Horrific customer service and quality controls. I drove two hours to buy emergency fruit fly cultures, only to have two of the three cultures release hundreds of FLYING fruit flies into my house when opened. The store reps I contacted first claimed that they “sell them like that,” before walking back that outlandish statement and claiming that I lied about receiving flying cultures. They then refused to issue a refund to my card unless I drove four hours round trip to show them the cultures. These cultures were already both more expensive and smaller than the industry-standard 32oz cultures. I would love to support a well-stocked reptile/amphibian store, but I’m not a glutton for faulty products and customer gaslighting. Spend your money elsewhere.

If you’re looking for a place that actually gives a damn about the animals they sell, you need to head over to Animal Ark. I’m at this shop all the time, and I can honestly say it’s the gold standard for exotic pet stores.

I recently got my baby bearded dragon from them, and the whole experience was incredible from start to finish. But honestly, what really sets this place apart from any other shop isn't just the amazing selection—it’s the people who work there. The staff has so much insight into every single animal in the building. You can tell they aren't just there to clock in; they have a genuine passion for what they do.

The vibe is what really keeps me coming back. It’s a total two-way street when it comes to knowledge. I’m constantly learning something new from them every time I walk through the doors, and they’re awesome enough to sit there and listen to my experiences, too. I teach them, they teach me—it’s a real community feel that you just don’t find at the big-box stores.

It’s rare to find a shop where the team takes the actual time to educate you and make sure you’re 100% set up for success before you walk out the door. They care more about the well-being of the animal than just making a quick sale. Whether you’ve been keeping reptiles for years or you’re looking to get your very first pet, you’re going to leave here feeling confident and supported.

Fantastic people, healthy animals, and a wealth of knowledge. If you’re anywhere near Kingwood, you have to check them out. They are doing things the right way!

This place needs to be shut down. They take awful care of the animals and reptiles in this establishment. Obviously not regularly cleaning the reptiles “enclosures” which are small plastic storage containers and I mean SMALL. I honestly don’t know how this place is still in business with the way they take care of the store and their customers. The last time I was in there they had someone deliver an order for supplies for the store. He couldn’t speak English very well and they were being very rude to his face and treating him less than but also proceeded to talk about him after he left. The older lady that I guess manages the store or seems somewhat in charge made some sort of racist joke to another employee and the younger one says “don’t be rude” while laughing and obviously poking fun at the poor guy. This isn’t the first time she’s rubbed me the wrong way. She also has a horrible attitude. Though not all employees are like this. Please stay far away from this place and take your business somewhere else. If they can’t treat humans with decency what makes you think they are treating the animals any better. It’s 100% not normal for these animals and reptiles to be dying or severely sick after buying them from this establishment. The smell of this place should tell you enough…pet stores smell but not like this.
